annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Mild kidney damage with normal/high eGFR (>=60 ml/min) and persistent proteinuria. Management delivered in primary care.
typicalComponents: Annual GP review and blood pressure check
Annual serum creatinine/eGFR and urine ACR tests
Cardiovascular risk optimization (statin, basic antihypertensives)
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: High: Effective BP and lifestyle control at Stage 1-2 prevents progression to Stage 4-5, saving up to £35,000+ per patient annually in avoided renal replacement therapy.

annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Mild to moderate loss of kidney function (eGFR 45-59 ml/min). Primary care management with structured monitoring.
typicalComponents: 6-monthly GP and practice nurse reviews
Twice-yearly renal blood panel and urine ACR
Cardio-renal protective pharmacotherapy (ACEi/ARB, SGLT2 inhibitor e.g., Dapagliflozin/Empagliflozin)
Annual lifestyle and diet guidance check
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: Significant: Progression delay at stage 3a preserves years of patient productivity and avoids secondary care referral escalation.

annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Moderate to severe loss of kidney function (eGFR 30-44 ml/min). Enhanced monitoring, potential joint renal clinic review.
typicalComponents: 3-4 primary care reviews per year
Specialist nephrology outpatient consultation (1st/follow-up)
Biochemical monitoring of bone mineral markers (calcium, phosphate, PTH) and bicarbonate
Renal dietitian referral
Cardiorenal medications
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: Crucial: Preventing transition to Stage 4/5 averts imminent pre-dialysis vascular surgery and intensive multidisciplinary care.

annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Severe loss of kidney function (eGFR 15-29 ml/min). Multi-disciplinary pre-dialysis preparation and management.
typicalComponents: Frequent nephrology outpatient attendances (every 2-3 months)
Anaemia management (Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents / ESAs and IV iron)
Specialist pre-dialysis education and shared decision making
Vascular access creation (arteriovenous fistula) or PD catheter insertion
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: High cost inflection point: Care costs quadruple compared to Stage 3b.

annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Kidney failure requiring renal replacement therapy (3 sessions/week in hospital or satellite dialysis unit).
typicalComponents: 156 haemodialysis sessions per year (~£155-£185/session NHS tariff)
Patient transport services
Specialist nephrology and nursing staffing
High-dose ESAs, phosphate binders, calcimimetics
Vascular access maintenance and hospital admissions for complications
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: Maximum: Largest clinical and economic burden on the NHS.

annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Home-based dialysis (CAPD or APD) with monthly specialist clinic reviews.
typicalComponents: Peritoneal dialysis fluids and automated cycler equipment delivery
Monthly home dialysis nurse reviews and outpatient clinics
Catheter care and peritonitis treatment episodes
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: Substantial: Saves ~£13,000/year compared to hospital haemodialysis, but still orders of magnitude higher than early stage prevention.

annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Kidney transplantation procedure, inpatient stay, and initial high-intensity immunosuppression.
typicalComponents: Transplant surgical procedure and organ retrieval
Inpatient surgical ward and ICU stay (7-14 days)
Induction immunosuppression (e.g. Basiliximab/ATG) and prophylactic anti-infectives
Bi-weekly outpatient monitoring during the first 3 months
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: Restores quality of life and is cost-saving compared to dialysis within 2-3 years.

annualDirectCostsByStage.description: Long-term functioning allograft with stable maintenance immunosuppression.
typicalComponents: Maintenance immunosuppression (Tacrolimus, Mycophenolate Mofetil, Prednisolone)
3-monthly transplant clinic reviews and therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM)
Routine surveillance blood panels and skin cancer screening
annualDirectCostsByStage.economicBenefitOfPrevention: Most cost-effective long-term replacement modality (£6,800/yr vs £38,500/yr for HD).
